leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply the useRef hook to create a mutable reference to a DOM element in a TypeScript React component.
Implement the useEffect hook to manage side effects and attach event listeners to the document.
Use TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of props for a custom hook, including optional parameters.
Construct a custom hook function that returns a ref object for attaching to DOM elements.
Execute conditional logic to check if a click event target is outside the referenced element.
Handle click events by defining an event handler function that triggers a callback when clicks occur outside the element.
Control component lifecycle by properly cleaning up event listeners in the useEffect cleanup function.
Utilize TypeScript generics to type the ref object for flexibility with different HTML element types.
Assign the created ref to a JSX element's ref attribute to establish the click boundary.
Invoke the custom hook within a functional component to implement click-outside detection behavior.
Modify the hook to accept configuration options such as excluding certain elements from triggering the callback.
Return the ref object from the custom hook so it can be attached to the target element in the component.
